en.title: Pick k Digits to Form the Largest Integer
en.description:
Given n decimal digits, choose exactly k of them while keeping their original order, to form the largest possible integer. Leading zeros are allowed in the choice, but the output does not keep leading zeros; output 0 if all chosen digits are zero.

The input format, examples, and test data are compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 100000); the second line contains n digits (0..9).
en.output: Output the answer as described; multiple results are separated by spaces, in order.
en.explanation: The example inputs and outputs follow the rules above directly; see the solution for the full algorithm.
hints: You may delete n−k digits. Maintain a monotonic stack: when a new digit is larger, pop the smaller digits at the end as long as deletions remain. Finally, take the first k digits.
